key_insight: A bispectrum-based invariant lattice representation removes unit-cell convention ambiguity and substantially improves prediction of lattice parameters from powder XRD data.
engineering_relevance: This offers a more reliable target representation for crystallography ML, improving robustness in materials characterization, inverse design, and structure-related prediction workflows.
method: Build a reciprocal-lattice representation from spherical-harmonic projections and summarize it with a lattice bispectrum.
Use the bispectrum as the ML target instead of directly regressing conventional cell parameters.
Invert the bispectrum with a dynamic programming approach to recover lattice parameters.
evidence_signal: On the MP-20 dataset, the same model architecture achieved lower errors with the bispectrum target, reducing length MAPE from 11.18% to 2.44% and angle MAPE from 12.74% to 3.07%; the approach was also benchmarked on Crystalyze and the experimental RRUFF dataset.
watch_item: Because the bispectrum inversion is algorithmic and the representation is tied to reciprocal-lattice sampling, performance may depend on numerical stability and how well the method generalizes to noisy or incomplete experimental XRD patterns.
paper_title: Learning Lattice Parameters from Powder X-Ray Diffraction Data Using Invariants
